title: SDK integration walkthrough - Lyra Finance
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Lyra Finance team through the Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, auth patterns (API key vs SSO), and environment setup. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated, VPC/KMS concerns for PII workloads, basic benchmarking plan, and next steps for a POC. Action items include sharing quickstart repos, SOC2 docs, and scheduling a benchmark run in early January.
topics: Auth and env vars / API keys vs SSO
Hosted vs Dedicated and VPC options
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing guidance
Share SOC 2 and ISO docs + network diagram
Jordan to provide TypeScript quickstart repo and sample app link
Lyra to provide sample data shape and target latency SLOs

Maya Patel - Send pricing sheet and Dedicated sizing deck - 2027-01-02
Maya Patel - Share SOC2/ISO certs and security playbook link - 2027-01-02

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Lyra CTO), Priya (Lead Engineer), Liam (Security), Ava (PM)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Jordan will walk through the SDK quickstarts and integration pattern.
[00:28] Jordan (Redwood SE): yep hi all glad to be here. quick agenda: show Python quickstart, TS quickstart, auth patterns, env vars, a bit on hosted vs dedicated and then Q&A. we'll try to keep it hands-on.
[01:15] Carlos (Lyra CTO): great, we have Priya who will actually do the hands-on later, and Liam from security for network/auth questions. our main asks: low latency for transactional scoring, keys/PII handling, and a clear path for a POC.
[02:05] Jordan (Redwood SE): understood. starting with the Python SDK: install via pip, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var, then example call to rclient.text.generate with model param. code sample link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python-quickstart (note: link in transcript may be slightly off).
[03:00] Priya (Lead Engineer): question, where do we store keys in our deploy? we use k8s secrets and HashiVault.
[03:18] Jordan (Redwood SE): that's totally fine. many customers use Vault or env vars via secrets. we also support per-route service principals if you want to rotate keys centrally. if you're on Private with KMS we can plug into customer KMS.
[04:15] Liam (Security): when you say KMS, is that customer-managed? we need HSM-backed keys and audit logs for every request.
[04:40] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, on Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) and detailed audit logs. hosted also has encryption at rest and key management, but for HSM-backed customer keys you would opt for Private or Dedicated with customer KMS.
[05:20] Maya (Redwood AE): to jump in — for Lyra's PII workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can work if you pseudonymize, but Dedicated gives more isolation and predictable throughput.
[06:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): back to SDK: TypeScript quickstart uses npm package @redwood/inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the browser token for frontend. server-side we recommend env vars or vault. sample repo (TS) I'll share after the call.
[07:10] Priya (Lead Engineer): any examples for streaming and function calling? we use streaming for partial responses to reduce latency.
[07:40] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes we have streaming examples. note on streaming: in Python you get a generator pattern, in TS you can use EventSource/Server-Sent Events too. small gotcha: make sure you set the content-type and use the wss endpoint for websockets in some regions.
[09:00] Carlos (CTO): around latency/cost tradeoffs, can you quantify typical tps on a Dedicated pool?
[09:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): ballpark depends on model and quantization. e.g., for a 7B quantized model we often see 40-60 qps per GPU with batching tuned; latency median under 150-200ms for short prompts. we'll need your prompt distribution to size properly.
[10:45] Priya (Lead Engineer): we also do embeddings for search, are those via a separate endpoint?
[11:05] Jordan (Redwood SE): embeddings endpoints are separate; SDK supports embed calls. batching and cache suggestions are in the Optimize tab in Console — you'll get recommendations automatically after some traffic.
[12:00] Maya (Redwood AE): quick note on quotas and rate limits — hosted free tiers have soft limits; Dedicated gives predictable throughput. we'll include a Dedicated sizing guide in the deck.
[15:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): demo time — I'm going to share my screen (audio: faint clicks). Python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxxx, then python example that calls client.generate. (some typing sounds)
[18:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): small transcription oddity in the recorder: K-V cache might show up as K-V cash, ignore that. prefix caching is important if you have repeated prefixes — we can save a lot on tokens.
[21:00] Priya (Lead Engineer): if we do private deployment in our VPC, is the control plane still managed?
[21:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, typically the control plane is customer-managed for Private, or we can do a hybrid where control plane is in your VPC. on Dedicated the control plane is hosted but we provide network peering and strict access.
[22:30] Liam (Security): SSO and RBAC — we need SAML for SSO and fine-grained RBAC for routes and secrets.
[22:55] Maya (Redwood AE): Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based permissions in the Console. we'll send docs for your security team.
[25:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): quick TS demo: npm i @redwood/inference, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then example using await client.responses.create({ model: 'rwd-7b', input: '...' }). show code snippet (brief pause).
[28:10] Priya (Lead Engineer): about environment variables, we run 12-factor apps so env is perfect, but rotate keys every 30 days — do you have built-in rotation?
[28:40] Jordan (Redwood SE): we recommend using Vault or cloud KMS for rotation. Hosted supports key rotation through our portal but for compliance customers often pair with Vault and use short-lived tokens.
[31:00] Carlos (CTO): can we control model rollouts between rwd-7b and rwd-3b for cost purposes? feature flags?
[31:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, Console supports per-route model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B). plus automatic fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.
[35:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): mention of Optimize: it will suggest batching, quantization profiles, and cost savings; we'll run that during the POC.
[39:00] Maya (Redwood AE): security ask — Liam are there specific docs you want first?
[39:20] Liam (Security): SOC2, ISO, network diagram, penetration test reports, encryption details, and manual on audit logs retention.
[39:45] Maya (Redwood AE): we'll send SOC2/ISO and network diagram; Jordan will include audit log retention notes in the security packet.
[41:30] Priya (Lead Engineer): let's talk POC: we want a benchmark that mirrors our transaction flow — sample payload size ~300 tokens, target p95 < 300ms.
[42:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): sounds reasonable. for benchmarking we'll spin up a dedicated pool in a sandbox, run synthetic traffic, capture latency and cost metrics. need your sample dataset and expected throughput.
[44:00] Carlos (CTO): timeline — can we start in first week of Jan?
[44:15] Maya (Redwood AE): yes, aim for week of 2027-01-10. I'll coordinate calendar invites.
[47:00] Jordan (Redwood SE): quick troubleshooting notes: if you see tokenization mismatch, ensure model tokenizer aligns and you pre-tokenize in SDK where possible. also note occasional ASR errors in auto-transcription with company names — ignore those.
[50:00] Ava (PM): what's the onboarding 90-day success criteria?
[50:20] Maya (Redwood AE): reduce inference cost per call by 30% vs current self-hosted, p95 latency < 300ms, and integration in staging with audit logs enabled. we'll formalize this in the POC doc.
[53:00] Priya (Lead Engineer): any recommended sample repos for us to clone?
[53:20] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes I'll share three links: Python quickstart repo, TypeScript sample app (server-side integration + streaming example), and a mini-bench harness.
[55:00] Maya (Redwood AE): recap of next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs, Jordan shares quickstart repos, Lyra provides sample dataset and SLOs, and we schedule the POC kickoff week of Jan 10.
[56:30] Carlos (Lyra CTO): thanks all, this was helpful. looking forward to the repos.
[56:45] Maya (Redwood AE): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email with links and calendar invites. talk soon.

Notes: transcript contains some auto-caption errors (company names, KV cache spelled K-V cash). references made to docs and repos will be provided as links in follow-up email.
